newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-AGA KHAN SENDS HORSES TO STOUTE AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-AGA KHAN SENDS HORSES TO STOUTE AGAIN.

text.p: One of horse racing's most successful partnerships is set to resume after confirmation on Tuesday that Michael Stoute will receive five yearlings to be trained for the Aga Khan before the end of the year.
Stoute and the Aga enjoyed a fruitful association before the owner withdrew his horses from Britain over the "Aliysa" affair of 1989.

Among the big-race victories they shared during the 1980s were Shergar's 10-length triumph in the 1981 Derby and the win in 1986 of Shahrastani, the only horse in Europe to beat Dancing Brave as a three-year-old.

Epsom ultimately brought about their split as the Stoute-trained Aliysa, first past the post in the 1989 Oaks, was disqualified after traces of the banned substance camphor were found in her urine sample.

Since withdrawing his horses from Stoute's and Luca Cumani's stables, 78 in total, in 1990, the Aga has concentrated both his breeding and training operations in France and Ireland through Chantilly trainer Alain de Royer Dupre and County Kildare trainer John Oxx.

However, after making his peace with the Jockey Club over its drug-testing procedures, the Aga announced last year that he would revive his involvment with British racing, and the Luca Cumani-trained Mandilak marked his return with a victory at Yarmouth a fortnight ago.
Newmarket-based Stoute said: "I am delighted at the Aga Khan's decision...
"While the initial numbers are small, in my conversations with the Aga Khan quality was a more important consideration than quantity."

The owner, who will send 32 yearlings to Oxx, 53 to de Royer Dupre and 14 to Cumani, said: "I am particularly happy to see my colours carried by horses trained in England featuring again on English racecourses."
